query: idempotency-key HTTP header convention RFC standard
title: draft ietf httpapi idempotency key header
snippet: The Idempotency-Key header is defined in an IETF draft — draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header, in the httpapi working group — and it has expired without becoming an RFC. It's a convention that Stripe popularised, that most payment and API platforms copied, and that has no normative document behind it.
claim: The Idempotency-Key header is a de facto convention popularized by Stripe but remains an expired IETF draft without normative status.

query: idempotency-key HTTP header convention RFC standard
title: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field
snippet: The HTTP Idempotency-Key request header field can be used to make non-idempotent HTTP methods such as POST or PATCH fault-tolerant. Idempotency-Key is an Item Structured Header. Its value MUST be a String. The idempotency key MUST be unique and MUST NOT be reused with another request with a different request payload.
claim: Idempotency-Key makes non-idempotent HTTP methods fault-tolerant with unique string values tied to request payloads.

topic: Idempotency key implementation in payment APIs
query: idempotency key stripe payment API design best practices
title: Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency
snippet: Idempotency is a web API design principle defined as the ability to apply the same operation multiple times without changing the result beyond the first try. An example is charging a customer money; accidentally calling it twice would lead to the customer being double-charged.
claim: Idempotency ensures repeated identical operations produce the same result, preventing duplicate charges in payment systems.

topic: Stripe idempotency key handling and TTL
query: idempotency key stripe payment API design best practices
title: Stripe Idempotency Keys: How They Work and When You Must Use Them
snippet: At the heart of Stripe's idempotency system is the Idempotency-Key header, which helps Stripe's servers recognize repeated requests and respond appropriately. A client generates a unique ID to identify just that operation and sends it up to the server along with the normal payload. Stripe stores idempotency keys for 24 hours. Don't use the same key across different user sessions or checkout attempts.
claim: Stripe stores idempotency keys for 24 hours and requires unique IDs per operation and user session.

query: idempotency-key HTTP header convention RFC standard
title: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field
snippet: It is RECOMMENDED that a UUID or a similar random identifier be used as an idempotency key. Uniqueness of the key MUST be defined by the resource owner and MUST be implemented by the clients of the resource.
claim: UUID or random identifiers are recommended for idempotency keys with uniqueness defined by resource owner.

title: Idempotency & Deduplication | System Design Sandbox
snippet: Start with idempotency keys at your API boundary to catch client-side retries, add message deduplication in your consumers to handle queue redeliveries, and use database constraints as your final safety net for critical operations.
claim: Robust idempotency requires keys at API boundary, deduplication in consumers, and database constraints for critical operations.

topic: Varying idempotency key retention windows across providers
query: idempotency-key HTTP header convention RFC standard
title: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field
snippet: While the header name is consistent across the industry, the semantics are whatever each provider decided, meaning retention windows, parameter-mismatch behaviour, and concurrency handling all differ between providers.
claim: Despite consistent header names, idempotency implementations vary by provider in retention windows and parameter handling.
